sources.quote: Guaranteed rankings, traffic or leads.** Nobody controls Google.
sources.title: Do You Need an SEO? Tips for Hiring an SEO | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: No one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google. Beware of SEOs that claim to guarantee rankings, allege a special relationship with Google, or advertise a priority submit to Google. There is no priority submit for Google.

sources.quote: You should see exactly what Google and Meta charged.
sources.title: Google third-party policy - Advertising Policies Help
sources.evidence: When sharing Google advertising cost data with customers, third parties must report the exact amount charged by Google, exclusive of any fees that they charge. If a third party charges a management fee, they must clearly inform customers in writing before each first purchase and disclose the fee on all customer invoices. Reporting must be provided no less than monthly, disclosing absolute dollars spent on Google.

sources.quote: CASL for email and SMS, Quebec's French-language rules
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: CASL takes a technology-neutral approach, so that all means of telecommunications are captured under the law, including Short Message Services (SMS or text messaging). An electronic address is defined in CASL as being: an email account, a telephone account, an instant messaging account, and any other similar accounts.

sources.quote: provincial privacy law, Canadian ad-platform policies
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.title: Provincial laws that may apply instead of PIPEDA - Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.evidence: Alberta, British Columbia and Quebec have their own private-sector privacy laws that have been deemed substantially similar to PIPEDA. Organizations subject to a substantially similar provincial privacy law are generally exempt from PIPEDA with respect to the collection, use or disclosure of personal information that occurs within that province.
